title: When modern human behaviour appeared
summary: One camp sees a sudden package of modern behaviour about 40,000–50,000 years ago; the view now gaining ground is a mosaic of traits emerging gradually in Africa's Middle Stone Age.
why: It asks when people became 'us' in mind, not just in body.

notes.problem: Source: behavioural modernity 'is increasingly understood as a mosaic of traits that emerged gradually'; summary should show the lean.

question: Did modern human behaviour, like art and symbols, appear suddenly or build up gradually?
evidence: Ochre and shell beads dated about 70,000–160,000 years ago in Africa; symbolic items also at Neanderthal sites; full package clear by 40,000–50,000 years ago.
wouldSettle: Securely dated symbolic artefacts showing whether traits accumulated steadily or appeared together.

theories.name: Upper Paleolithic Revolution
theories.idea: A sudden cognitive change about 50,000 years ago in Africa preceded the spread out of Africa.

theories.name: Gradual mosaic
theories.idea: Modern behaviours accumulated over a long period in Africa's Middle Stone Age.

theories.name: Shared with Neanderthals
theories.idea: Symbolic behaviour such as pigment use also appears among Neanderthals, so it is not unique to us.
